references.text: The breastpiece (חֹשֶׁן) is first mentioned here as part of the high priest's holy garments that were to be made.
The ephod is described with the same materials: gold, blue and purple wool, scarlet yarn, and finely twisted linen - identical craftsmanship to the breastpiece.
The breastpiece is called 'the breastpiece of judgment' (חֹשֶׁן מִשְׁפָּט) because it contained the Urim and Thummim, which were used to seek the Lord's judgment and guidance.
Fulfillment of the command - the breastpiece was made exactly as commanded, with skilled workmanship and the same materials.
Moses placed the breastpiece on Aaron during the consecration of the priesthood and put the Urim and Thummim in it.
The skilled workmanship (מַעֲשֵׂה חֹשֵׁב) is also used for the tabernacle curtains, which were made from the same materials.
The same materials - blue, purple, scarlet, and fine linen - were given as offerings for the construction of the sanctuary.
Highlights the unity in the priest's clothing by showing that both the breastpiece and the belt require identical skilled workmanship and materials.
Confirms that the ephod (which the breastpiece is to match) is made from the same holy materials.
Thematic parallel between the priest's breastpiece and the tabernacle curtain: both bear the same colors symbolizing God's presence.
